name: Citizenship by Birth and by Descent

requirement_groups.name: Born on the island of Ireland with a qualifying parent

requirements.blocker_text: For births on/after 1 January 2005 on the island of Ireland, this requires at least one parent who is Irish/British, an EEA/UK national with unrestricted residence, or a parent with 3 years' reckonable residence in the 4 years before the birth (student/asylum time excluded). Births before 1 January 2005 were automatically Irish regardless of parental status. A child otherwise stateless is granted citizenship.

requirement_groups.name: Child born abroad to a parent born on the island of Ireland

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a parent who was born on the island of Ireland — citizenship is automatic; just apply for a passport, no Foreign Births Register entry needed.

requirement_groups.name: Grandchild via Foreign Births Register (distinctive Irish provision)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a grandparent born on the island of Ireland, even if neither parent was ever born in or resident in Ireland — but MUST register on the Foreign Births Register; citizenship dates from the registration itself, not from birth.
requirements.fix_path: Complete Foreign Births Register registration with the Department of Foreign Affairs.

requirements.blocker_text: This further generation only works if the LINKING parent registered on the Foreign Births Register BEFORE the applicant's own birth — the chain must be maintained generation by generation; there is no entitlement beyond this.

evidence_required.document: Birth/parentage documentation matching the applicable group
Foreign Births Register application (grandchild and further-generation groups)

sources.title: Irish citizenship - Citizens Information (state-funded service, citing primary legislation)

notes: GENUINE, DISTINCTIVE IRISH PROVISION worth flagging as one of the most generous ancestry mechanisms in this entire multi-country dataset: the Foreign Births Register grandparent rule works EVEN IF NEITHER PARENT was ever born in or resident in Ireland — a materially more generous reach-back than Portugal's post-2025 parent/grandparent-only cap (which at least requires a direct parent-or-grandparent link with additional conditions) or most other ancestry routes in this dataset. Citizenship dates from the REGISTRATION itself, not from birth — a real and consequential distinction, since it means the FBR applicant is not retroactively Irish for the period before registration. The further-generation (great-grandchild) case is genuinely chain-dependent: it ONLY works if the linking parent registered on the FBR before the applicant's own birth — this is a real structural limit that prevents indefinite generational reach, distinct from a true unlimited-generations system. Post-2005 birthright citizenship (Group 1) reflects Ireland's 2004 constitutional amendment tightening automatic jus soli — a genuine historical parallel to Portugal's 2025 jure sanguinis tightening and the ongoing US birthright-citizenship litigation covered elsewhere in this dataset, though Ireland's change is long-settled (2005) rather than currently contested.
